title: Can apps teach you a language?
reason: 近期课程已覆盖拒绝应对、职场压力、消费与记忆，今天轮换到软件和数字学习。本集比较语言学习应用与课堂在重复练习、语法讲解和听力提升上的不同作用，直接对应‘能看懂却难以及时调用’的学习瓶颈，也适合从平台产品效果、证据边界和组合方案的角度思考。练习通过客观题反复激活高频搭配，再逐步撤掉支架进入工作与学习场景。

targetExpressions.meaning: know or recognise something because you have seen or experienced it before
targetExpressions.usage: Use it to describe existing knowledge: Many learners are familiar with short app-based lessons.

targetExpressions.meaning: experience or come into contact with something regularly
targetExpressions.usage: Use it for repeated contact with language or ideas: Children are constantly exposed to the language around them.

targetExpressions.meaning: a combination of two or more different things
targetExpressions.usage: Use it when several methods work together: A mixture of app practice and direct teaching can be useful.

targetExpressions.meaning: the most important conclusion or discovery from research
targetExpressions.usage: Use it to report evidence clearly: The key finding was that the two groups improved in different skills.

targetExpressions.meaning: use or join two things together
targetExpressions.usage: Use it to build a balanced plan: Combine app exercises with speaking practice.

targetExpressions.meaning: discover the method that is effective for your own needs
targetExpressions.usage: Use it when the best choice depends on the person: Try several study methods and find what works for you.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the sentence from the discussion: Many listeners might ______ how language-learning apps tend to work.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Neil says listeners might be familiar with how the apps tend to work: short lessons test a repeated set of words.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: In the episode, what does it mean for a child to be constantly “exposed to” language?

options.text: The child regularly hears and experiences language in daily life.
The child studies only written grammar rules.
The child avoids language until formal lessons begin.
The child tests one language app for a few hours.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: Professor Wonnacott contrasts children, who are constantly exposed to a world of language, with adults studying only a few hours a week.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the conclusion: For adults, ______ implicit app learning and explicit teaching can be useful.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Pippa says that a mixture of the apps' implicit teaching and explicit teaching, such as grammar rules, is useful.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Which option accurately states the study's key finding?

options.text: App learners improved more on some written grammar tests, while classroom learners improved more in listening.
App learners improved more than classroom learners in every tested skill.
Classroom learners improved only because they studied for longer.
Neither group showed any improvement in grammar or listening.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The transcript reports different strengths: the app group improved a little more on some written grammar tests, while the classroom group appeared to improve more in listening.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete Neil's recommendation: Learners should ______ app learning ______ other ways of studying.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Neil says the best approach is to combine learning in apps with other ways of studying because the app group was less successful in listening.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: What does the advice “find what works for you” encourage learners to do?

options.text: Choose and combine methods that effectively develop their own skills.
Use the same app and routine as every other learner.
Stop practising skills that are difficult to measure.
Rely on implicit learning and avoid direct explanations.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The teachers suggest practising different skills through podcasts, speaking partners and apps, then choosing the combination that is effective for the individual.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: According to the programme, which language could not be learned on Duolingo at the time?
objectiveQuestions.explanation: The quiz answer is Elvish; the programme says Latin and Klingon were available on Duolingo.

options.text: I combine vocabulary review with a weekly conversation.
I combine with vocabulary review a weekly conversation with.
I combine vocabulary review to a weekly conversation.
I am combine vocabulary review by a weekly conversation.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The natural pattern is combine one thing with another thing, as in the episode's recommendation to combine apps with other study methods.

assessment.retellingPrompt: Without looking at the full transcript, retell the episode in 80–120 words using this structure: (1) topic—how language apps teach and why they are convenient; (2) evidence—the difference between children's exposure and adult study, plus the app-versus-class study result; (3) conclusion—a balanced way to practise different skills. Phrase bank: “be exposed to”, “key finding”, “combine ... with ...”. Use at least two phrases naturally. Simple, accurate sentences are enough.
referencePoints: Language apps often use short lessons, repeated words and implicit learning rather than directly explaining every rule.
Children are constantly exposed to their first language, while adults may study a new language for only a few hours a week.
Some explicit teaching of grammar and vocabulary is helpful for adult learners.
In one study, app learners improved a little more on some written grammar tests, while classroom learners appeared to improve more in listening.
The study was promising but limited to one language, one app and one school.
The programme recommends combining apps with human teaching and activities that practise speaking, listening, reading and writing.
